rounds.text: T & I Global Ltd offers an exceptionally conservative balance sheet, operating completely debt-free with borrowings at zero [E37, E38]. This strong financial foundation translates into remarkable cash generation, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs 19 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs 18 Cr for Mar 2026, supported by an impressive cash conversion ratio of 2.71x that proves profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34, E35, E36]. Furthermore, working capital management has improved dramatically, with requirements dropping from 57.7 days to just 14.1 days [E50]. Valuation multiples also present an attractive entry point, with the stock trading at a price-to-book ratio of 0.96x against its book value of ₹ 195 [E2], alongside a discounted EV/EBITDA of 8.28x relative to its sector benchmark of 12.26x [E11]. Recent operational momentum is accelerating strongly, demonstrated by trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 18% and an extraordinary 84% jump in compounded profit growth [E17, E21], all while benefiting from a broader Capital Goods sector tailwind with a score of +0.62 [E64]. conceded: [E42]

The valuation is unsupported by intrinsic fundamentals, evidenced by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 130 per share against a market price of Rs 188, leaving a negative margin of safety of 44.5% [E42, E43]. This overvaluation is confirmed by a rules-based screen score of 41 out of 100 resulting in a medium-confidence sell rating [E55]. Furthermore, profitability and capital efficiency metrics lag sector benchmarks considerably, with a return on equity of 7.06% versus a sector benchmark of 11.28%, and a return on capital employed of 9.62% against 12.85% [E9, E10]. Long-term growth has been persistently weak, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 2% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -7% [E14, E19]. Operating margins have also compressed, falling by 4 percentage points in the trailing twelve months to 3% from 7% three years earlier, alongside a recent quarterly margin drop to 8% in June 2026 from 12% in the year-ago quarter [E30, E31]. Additionally, earnings quality is called into question by the inclusion of Rs 5.59 Cr in other income [E54], and the company pays a dividend yield of 0.00% despite reporting profits [E4, E51]. Conceded: the company maintains a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and achieved strong free cash flow of Rs 18 Cr in March 2026 [E36, E37].

While the bear relies on a DCF model giving an intrinsic value of Rs 130 [E42, E43] and a low screen score [E55], these static models ignore accelerating fundamental momentum, including an 18% compounded sales growth in the trailing twelve months and an 84% surge in compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. The bear's concern over lower ROE and ROCE [E9, E10] is countered by the company's pristine financial health, maintaining a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x alongside a robust free cash flow of Rs 18 Cr and outstanding cash conversion of 2.71x for March 2026 [E34, E36, E37]. Conceded: the company delivered a 5-year compounded profit growth of -7% and a 10-year compounded sales growth of just 2% [E14, E19]. However, working capital efficiency has dramatically improved, with requirements dropping from 57.7 days to 14.1 days [E50]. Finally, the business benefits from trading near its book value at 0.97x compared to a sector benchmark of 2.39x, while operating within a Capital Goods sector experiencing a strong tailwind score [E7, E64].

The bull highlights accelerating 18% TTM sales growth and an 84% TTM profit surge [E17, E21], but these short-term metrics stand in stark contrast to long-term stagnation, including a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -6% and 5-year profit decline of -7% [E16, E19]. Conceded: the company maintains a 0.00x debt-to-equity ratio alongside Rs 18 Cr in free cash flow and a 2.71x cash conversion for March 2026 [E34, E36, E37]. However, this pristine balance sheet fails to generate adequate returns, as evidenced by a low 3-year median ROE of 7% and a 7.06% ROE that significantly lags the sector benchmark of 11.28% [E9, E28]. While the bull points to improved working capital efficiency and a P/B of 0.97x against a sector benchmark of 2.39x [E7, E50], the rules-based screen scores the stock at a weak 41 out of 100 with a sell recommendation [E55]. Furthermore, earnings are artificially inflated by Rs 5.59 Cr in other income [E54], and the discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of just Rs 130 per share, leaving a negative margin of safety of -44.5% at the current market price of Rs 188 [E42, E43].
